Commentary.Commentary: Afghanistan will be confident they can get a result today itself. Rahmat Shah's century early on helped them cut down the trail but it was Alam's knock that helped them get a massive lead. He along with the tail grinded hard to score runs. Lunch has been taken. A big post-lunch session coming up. Stay tuned.

Just what Zimbabwe needed! They have bowled out the visitors but need 278 runs to win which could be tricky as the pitch has started to detiorate. Good session for the hosts though. Anything under 300 means they have chance to win here. Blessing Muzarabani was the star for them. His extra bounce did troubled the opposition and have ended with six-fer. Richard Ngarava was solid as well, he ended with three wickets.

OUT! TAKEN! There is the final wicket and it is Blessing Muzarabani wbo gets it. A short one on middle. Yamin looks to fend it but it gets big on him. It hits the splice and lobs to first slip. Simple catch.

Shah's blistering innings along with Alam has helped Afghanistan take the lead of 205 runs. Alam is still unbeaten on 64 and has Rashid for company. Afghanistan still have plenty of batting left and could try and stretch the lead past 350. Zimbabwe, to stay in the game need to take remaining wickets quickly. The first hour could be massive. Whoever dominates could be the favourites to win the game. For now, it's the visitors but you cannot write the hosts yet. Stay tuned.

Afghanistan are likely to add more runs to their total on Day 4, further swelling their lead. This will leave Zimbabwe facing a monumental task, as they'll have to bat last on a wearing pitch against a high-quality Afghan bowling unit. Goodbye and do join us tomorrow.

Zimbabwe's bowlers were largely disciplined, but their fielding let them down, with several catches being dropped. These missed opportunities proved costly, as Afghanistan capitalized on them to build a substantial lead. As the game stands, Afghanistan are firmly in the driver's seat, and Zimbabwe will need to produce a remarkable turnaround to salvage the match.

Rain has the final say as it is stumps on Day3 of this Test match and it belonged to Afghanistan, who staged a remarkable turnaround to take control of the game. Starting the day trailing by 40 runs, Afghanistan ended it with a lead of 205 runs. Rahmat Shah was the star of the show, scoring a magnificent century to anchor the Afghan innings. He received excellent support from debutant Ismat Alam, who notched up a brilliant half-century.

Otherwise, the Zimbabwean bowlers struggled to make an impact, and the game is slowly slipping away from them. With Afghanistan's lead continuing to grow, Zimbabwe desperately needs to find a way to increase their productivity with the ball.

Rahmat Shah was once again the star of the session, anchoring the innings well. He stays at 105 not out and has received able support from Ismat Alam, who remained unbeaten on 31. The pair's partnership has put Afghanistan in a strong position, leaving Zimbabwe with a daunting task ahead.
The post-lunch session also belonged to Afghanistan, who continued to dominate Zimbabwe. They added 78 runs to their total, stretching their lead to 117, while losing only one wicket in this session.

Commentary.Commentary: As the game heads into day three, Afghanistan still trails by 40 runs with only seven wickets remaining. Rahmat Shah remains at the crease, shouldering the responsibility of guiding his team to a competitive total. Zimbabwe will aim to seize control on day three by taking early wickets and tightening their grip on the match. Exciting times ahead as we move closer to the start of play on Day 3.

Zimbabwe has dominated the opening two days of play, outperforming Afghanistan in all aspects. The hosts bowled out Afghanistan for a modest 157 runs in the first innings. In response, Zimbabwean batters capitalized on the momentum, scoring 243 themselves. This 86-run lead had given Zimbabwe a significant advantage. Their bowlers in the second inning once again ran through the visitor's top order, leaving them 46 for 3 at the end of the second day's play.
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

Earlier in the day, the Afghanistan bowlers fought back strongly and had Zimbabwe in trouble at 119 for 6. Ervine and Williams though batted brilliantly and helped their side take a decent lead. In reply, Zimbabwe have managed to get three wickets and they still lead by 40. They would hope they can continue taking wickets on Day 3. Afghanistan on the other hand, need a couple of partnership. Their first aim though will be to get past the deficit without any damage. Day 3 could indicate big time as to which way the game heads. Do join us for it. Till then, goodbye and take care!

After taking a lead of just over 80, they got around 15 overs to bowl to Afghanistan and they have managed to get three big wickets in those many overs. Blessing Muzarabani got two and Raza got the big wicket of Shahidi.

The umpires get together, have a chat and then decide the light is not good enough and off they go! That will be STUMPS and it is a day dominated by the hosts! They are in a very good position in this game.
